name: AL-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about 17 points Republican, among the reddest in the country
Incumbent Gary Palmer holds a roughly 33-to-1 fundraising advantage over Maurice Mercer
Prediction markets price Republican win probability near 96%, with no outside spending against Palmer
No general-election polls or expert ratings exist, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Palmer's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and market pricing near 96% Republican all point to a comfortable hold, while the Democratic challenger's minimal resources leave no visible path to competitiveness.
model.watch: Only an unexpected scandal involving Palmer or a sudden influx of outside spending against him would put the result in any doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 6th District is firmly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 17 points toward the GOP. Gary Palmer, the incumbent, was renominated without difficulty and holds a decisive financial edge, having raised about $1.15 million to Maurice Mercer's $35,000. No outside groups are spending against Palmer, and no general-election polls have been conducted in the race.

Prediction markets give Palmer roughly a 96% chance of re-election, and no expert raters list the contest as competitive. With a Republican-friendly national environment and a challenger lacking both money and name recognition, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin. The real uncertainty is the size of the winning margin, not which party prevails.
